Army historical accounts place its maximum speed at roughly 20 miles per hour, and its operating range at around 400 miles. Those figures would be unimpressive for an ordinary highway truck. But the TC497 was not built for an ordinary highway. Its entire purpose was to go where the highway did not exist. But building a machine this long created a problem that had nothing to do with horsepower. How do you make it turn? A normal truck pulling a trailer does not trace one perfect path around a corner.
